beats.text: In April 1921, a fisherman on Hatteras Island said he had found a bottle on the beach, with a note inside.
The note said a missing schooner's crew had been captured by an oil burning boat, and were being held prisoner.
That schooner, the Carroll A. Deering, had been found aground with every sail set and nobody aboard.
Five government departments were investigating. The note looked like the answer.
Then handwriting experts concluded the fisherman wrote it himself. He admitted it. He had hoped to land a job at the lighthouse.
The only clue pointing to a crime was invented. The eleven men were never found.
